technique: Hands on a bench behind you, feet on the floor (or elevated for harder variants); bend elbows to lower, then extend.
Keep hips close to the bench; use a modest ROM if shoulders complain.
setup: Stable bench; shoulders away from ears.
commonMistakes: Going too deep into shoulder extension
safety: Bench dips often use large shoulder extension — prefer shallow ROM or parallel-bar progressions if shoulders are irritable (McKenzie et al. 2020/2022).

evidenceRefs.label: McKenzie et al. 2020 — glenohumeral extension risk considerations in the dip
McKenzie et al. 2022 — bench vs bar vs ring dip kinematics and muscle activity
Suprak et al. 2011 — % body mass supported in push-up positions (~69–75% traditional)
NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (technique/safety norms)

bodyweightFraction.rationale: Feet remain on the floor, so net upper-limb load is well below a suspended dip. No dip-specific GRF study located; estimate informed by Suprak et al. modified push-up range (~54–62% BM) as an analogy for feet-supported upper-body pressing.
